title: In vivo organ-specific migration of apoptotic splenocytes in mice with colitis
author: Braun, Zeiser

steps.title: Place mice on chlorophyll‑free diet
steps.instruction: Feed both donor (CD45.1) and recipient (CD45.2) C57BL/6 mice (7–10 weeks old) a chlorophyll‑free diet for ~14 days before imaging to reduce background fluorescence.

steps.title: Euthanize donor and harvest spleen
steps.instruction: Euthanize donor CD45.1 mice by cervical dislocation (or approved method), remove spleen and mash through a 100 µm cell strainer into a 6 cm dish containing 5 mL 1X PBS.

steps.title: Lyse erythrocytes
steps.instruction: Spin cells at 300 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 2 mL erythrocyte lysis buffer (e.g., ACK) and incubate 20–25 °C for 2 min; add 40 mL 1X PBS, spin again at 300 × g for 5 min at 4 °C and discard supernatant.

steps.title: Resuspend splenocytes in cRPMI
steps.instruction: Resuspend the washed splenocytes in complete RPMI (cRPMI) to a concentration of 5 × 10⁶ cells/mL.

steps.title: Perform Extracorporeal Photopheresis (ECP)
steps.instruction: Plate 12 mL of the cell suspension per 10 cm dish, add 8‑methoxypsoralen (UVADEX) to a final concentration of 200 ng/mL and incubate 30 min at 37 °C in the dark; then expose cells to UVA at 2.0 J/cm² using a BS‑02 chamber (Opsytec) in dose‑controlled mode; wash cells twice with 1X PBS; resuspend up to 2.5 × 10⁸ cells/mL in 2 mL 1X PBS in a 50 mL tube. Total ECP treatment, staining and transplantation takes ~3 h.

steps.title: Label splenocytes with VivoTrack680
steps.instruction: Dissolve one vial of VivoTrack680 in 1.3 mL warm (37 °C) 1X PBS, vortex until clear (yielding 2 mL labeling solution); add 2 mL labeling solution to 2 mL cell suspension and vortex immediately; incubate 15 min at 20–25 °C in the dark; wash cells by adding 20 mL 1X PBS (20–25 °C) containing 1 % FCS or cRPMI, then wash two additional times with 1X PBS (20–25 °C) containing 1 % FCS, and finally wash two times with 1X PBS (20–25 °C) without additive.

steps.title: Transplant labeled splenocytes
steps.instruction: Resuspend the washed cells in 1X PBS to 5 × 10⁷ cells/mL and inject 200 µL (1 × 10⁷ cells) intravenously via tail‑vein; one donor mouse provides enough cells for two recipient mice; ensure 8‑MOP and UVA were applied together to induce apoptosis.

steps.title: Ex vivo fluorescence imaging of organs
steps.instruction: Open Living Image software and initialize the Lumina III system (≈1 h); euthanize recipient (CD45.2) mice, excise tumor and colon, remove residual fat and Peyer’s patches, clear colon of feces with PBS; tap colon on paper tissue, place samples on a black surface, photograph to centre them; set imaging parameters for VivoTrack680: excitation 640 nm, emission 710 nm, exposure auto, binning medium, F/Stop 2, lamp level high, field of view D, object height 1.5 cm; capture fluorescence images for colon and tumor; include control animals that did not receive fluorescent cells to define autofluorescence; avoid imaging in clear plastic dishes or with samples immersed in PBS.

steps.title: Digest tumor and isolate lymphocytes
steps.instruction: Weigh each tumor; add 5 mL warm (37 °C) tumor digestion medium to a 15 mL tube, chop tumor into small pieces and incubate at 37 °C with shaking at 200–300 rpm; pass digested tissue through a 100 µm strainer into a 50 mL tube and wash filter with 25 mL 1X PBS; spin at 400 × g for 10 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 3 mL Percoll 30 % (P30); layer Percoll gradients in a 15 mL tube: 3 mL Percoll 70 % (P70), carefully add 4 mL Percoll 40 % (P40), then 3 mL P30 containing the cell suspension; centrifuge at 680 × g for 20 min at 20–25 °C (acceleration 2, no brake); aspirate and discard the top phase and the upper half of the second phase, collect the lymphocyte band above the bottom phase, transfer to a 50 mL tube, add 25 mL 1X PBS and spin at 500 × g for 10 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant and resuspend cells in PBS for downstream FACS. Approximate digestion time ~2 h.

steps.title: FACS staining – viability and surface markers
steps.instruction: Distribute dissociated lamina propria and tumor lymphocyte samples into 96‑well round‑bottom plates; spin at 500 × g for 3 min at 4 °C and discard supernatant; add 100 µL LIVE/DEAD Fixable Aqua (1:1000 in 1X PBS) and incubate 15 min at 4 °C; wash twice with 200 µL flow cytometry staining buffer (spin 500 × g 3 min 4 °C); add 50 µL Fc block (anti‑mouse CD16/CD32, 1:25 in buffer) and incubate 10 min at 4 °C; add 50 µL surface antibody mix (total volume 100 µL): for Panel 1 add anti‑mouse CD45.1 (FITC) and CD45.2 (Pacific Blue) each 1:50 (final 1:100); for Panel 2 add anti‑mouse CD45.2 (PE) 1:50 (final 1:100) and anti‑mouse CD11b (FITC) 1:10 (final 1:20); incubate 30 min at 4 °C; wash twice with 200 µL buffer (500 × g 3 min 4 °C). For Panel 1 resuspend cells in 150 µL buffer, keep at 4 °C in the dark and acquire within 1 h. For Panel 2 resuspend in 200 µL BD Cytofix/Cytoperm, incubate 40 min at 4 °C, spin at 750 × g for 3 min at 4 °C, wash twice with 200 µL BD Perm/Wash (750 × g 3 min 4 °C), add 100 µL intracellular stain (anti‑mouse/human Arginase‑1 eFluor450, 1:50 in Perm/Wash) and incubate 30 min at 4 °C, wash twice with 200 µL Perm/Wash, resuspend in 150 µL Perm/Wash; add 10 µL counting beads to each sample and vortex before acquisition. Total staining procedure ~3 h.

steps.title: Acquire and analyze flow cytometry data
steps.instruction: Run samples on a flow cytometer (Panel 1 within 1 h, Panel 2 can be kept at 4 °C up to 24 h); export data as .fcs files; in FlowJo (or equivalent) gate sequentially on all events, counting beads, singlets, live cells, CD45.2⁺ recipient cells, optionally exclude CD45.1⁺ donor cells, then gate on VivoTrack680⁺ cells; export counts of beads and CD45.2⁺ VivoTrack680⁺ cells; calculate total cell numbers per sample using the bead‑based formula provided by the manufacturer; normalize to tissue weight (cells per mg) using the pre‑digestion tumor weight.

steps.title: Analyze ex vivo imaging data
steps.instruction: In Living Image software import fluorescence images, perform spectral unmixing using autofluorescence control tissues and tissues from splenocyte‑transferred mice; define regions of interest (ROI) and record average radiant efficiency (p/s/cm²/sr per µW/cm²); for representative figures adjust the color scale so that control tissue shows no color; this analysis typically requires 1–2 h.

description: This protocol describes the specific steps to identify in vivo migration and phagocytic uptake of splenocytes treated with Extracorporeal Photopheresis (ECP) in C57BL/6 mice transplanted with s.c. melanoma and immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-induced colitis. ECP treatment renders splenocytes apoptotic. We use male and female C57BL/6N (CD45.2, Janvier Labs) and CD45.1 (Charles River) mice with an age of 7–10 weeks in the following protocol. We transplant recipient (CD45.2) and donor (CD45.1) mice subcutaneously with syngeneic B16.F10 melanoma cells and treat them with Dextran Sodium Sulfate (DSS, colitis grade) and anti-PD-1 to induce ICI-associated colitis. Colitis following ICI is one of the major limitations of ICI in the context of cancer therapy. Anti-CTLA-4 could be used as an alternative ICI, and tumor induction could also be achieved using other established syngeneic murine tumor cell lines. Previously, we have established ECP as an immunomodulatory therapy for ICI-induced colitis in mice and humans. ECP describes the treatment of immune cells with 8-methoxypsoralen and UVA, thereby inducing apoptosis in these cells. In our preclinical model, we have established splenocytes as the immune cell source for ECP therapy (see Braun et al., 20251). To discriminate recipient and donor immune cells in organ analysis, we transfer splenocytes from CD45.1 donor mice into CD45.2 recipient mice. The donor and recipient mice are treated similarly; this includes transplantation with syngeneic tumor, and treatment with DSS and anti-PD-1. ECP-treated splenocytes are stained with a fluorescent dye to track the migration of the cells into specific organs using an IVIS Lumina III imaging system. It is important to apply a chlorophyll-free diet to the mice for ∼14 days before the imaging experiment to reduce the background fluorescence.
